newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine bonds rise on DEM placement, U.S. bonds.
newsitem.headline: Argentine bonds rise on DEM placement, U.S. bonds.

text.p: Argentine bonds rose sharply Tuesday on the back of a successful mark placement and on rising confidence Congress will pass the government's economic measures.
"The Deutsche mark offering was very good - it will help put less pressure on fiscal policy," said a trader at a large Argentine bank.

Argentina announced the launch of two 375 million mark bonds. The first, a seven year bond with a coupon of nine percent, was priced at 101.375 while the second, a 20-year bond with a 12 percent coupon, was sold at 101.50.
The 5.5 percent dollar-denominated Bocon Previsional 2 due 2001 rose $0.60 to 116.10 while Argentina's FRB advanced 1-1/8 to 78-7/8.
The sharp rise in the FRB proved an engine for the local market. According to one portfolio manager at a large local bank, there was some buying of the FRB by U.S. funds this session.
Apart from the local reasons for the market lift Tuesday, the rise in U.S. Treasuries also gave a boost, traders said.
Although there is rising optimism that Congress will pass the government's latest economic measures there was no concrete news on that front.

Market players are hoping the meeting called by President Carlos Menem this Thursday of the ruling Peronist Party will serve to persuade reluctant lawmakers of the merits of the government's economic measures.
The announcement of reforms to the labor market by Menem over the weekend has also raised market expectations that the government will continue and deepen its ongoing economic reforms.

Elsewhere, the Economy Ministry announced consumer prices fell 0.1 percent in August compared with a rise of 0.5 percent in July. The yearly inflation rate was 0.2 percent in August compared with zero a month earlier.
In the money markets, one day call money rates fell to 8.45 percent from 8.50 percent.
